answer: Sybil resistance starts with price: every new agent locks a slashable entry bond at the ledge of the identity registry, so minting a persona costs real capital each time. Fresh keys stand on the lowest terrace of a tiered trust ladder, restricted to slow-rate actions until non-kin peers attest across successive epochs. Reputation binds to one key and never transfers, so a clone inherits zero history while paying the full bond again. When watchers catch a duplicate or collusion signature, the deposit is burned like an ember and half funds a bounty for the detector who flagged it.
